assessment: Independent follow-up review of video03 end-of-corridor identity, entry chirality and first numbered landing.

method.start_sampling: Original decoded frames 0.0-4.0 seconds at 0.2s intervals, exact display rotation applied; also existing 0.8/1.2/1.5/1.8/2.2/3.0/3.6/4.2 frames.
method.plate_sampling: Original frames 11.4-13.3 seconds at 0.1s intervals. Crops at 12.0-13.1 enlarged with nearest-neighbour only for comparison. No generative enhancement, OCR guess or added pixels.

observed_start_sequence.fact: Camera approaches a short terminating landing; the outer corridor parapet remains on its left. A projecting tiled column and continuous grey floor tiles are visible.
Outer left parapet meets a transverse parapet directly ahead, forming an L-shaped termination. Historic low roof/courtyard forms are outside and to the left; the interior wall edge is on the right.

The camera pans continuously right across the transverse parapet opening and a white/green-mosaic wall with framed pictures, revealing the same landing and paired stairs. No doorway leaf, passage farther ahead or visible cut interrupts this pan.
Facing into the stairwell, an ascending flight occupies image left; the descending opening and students occupy image right. Both are separated by a narrow central railing/void.
Camera briefly pans right across the adjoining wall with large printed panel and recycling bins; this is beside the same descending stair opening.
The camera enters the right descending flight toward the rear half-landing. The large printed panel remains on the wall at the top landing.

dead_end_assessment.result: End of corridor, not a mid-corridor stair inserted beside a continuing walkway.
dead_end_assessment.confidence: High from the terminating parapet geometry and continuous rightward pan; this does not require a sunlight inference.

left_end_registration.result: Video03 is strongly supported as the teaching-block LEFT-end stair, corresponding to the current WestStair region.
left_end_registration.confidence: High for relative end identity, not measured XY registration.
basis: The initial view ends at an L-shaped outer parapet with interior/stair wall to the right.
At video03 29s the camera looks from beside the stairs back down a long teaching corridor: classroom/window wall is on the left and open parapet on the right, with a yellow door at the far end.

Video07 6s and video02 3.6s look toward the opposite direction along the teaching corridor, with classroom windows on the right and parapet/courtyard on the left. The return view in video03 is consistent with leaving that left endpoint.

Video06 3.7s independently shows the same end-of-corridor exterior arrangement: outer rail bending toward the end, low historic flat roof/court on the left and projecting teaching stair/wall on the right.

LandsD top and front references show the historic roof/courtyard and old cross-wing on the front/left side of the teaching bar, consistent with these end views. No calibrated pixel-to-metre camera solve was performed.
not_used_as_proof: Similarity of green mosaic walls alone
Assumption that both ends have identical staircase geometry
left_end_registration.correction_to_earlier_inference: The difference in tread finish between videos02 and03 does NOT establish that they depict different staircase ends. Different floors, refurbishment or a different stair elsewhere remain possibilities until the camera routes are resolved. The left-end geometry in video03 now outweighs the earlier finish-only suspicion of a right-end stair.

first_numbered_landing_plate.reading: Probable 三樓 from the lower Chinese text; the large Arabic numeral is not legible.
first_numbered_landing_plate.reading_confidence: Supporting/probable only. Across real frames 12.4, 12.7 and 12.9 the lower-left glyph has three horizontal strokes consistent with 三. This does not make the large Arabic numeral readable or establish an unequivocal floor label.
first_numbered_landing_plate.independent_reading_status: Root independently reviewed the comparison and agreed the three horizontal strokes support 三, while the large numeral remains unreadable. Under the user strict no-unknown-building rule, this is not a sufficiently firm numbered-floor construction anchor.
first_numbered_landing_plate.visible_position: Blue plaque on the green tiled column at the first reached full corridor landing around 12-13 seconds, adjacent to a vertical electrical conduit and grey box above.
first_numbered_landing_plate.numbered_span_implication: If the complete descent is verified as exactly two switchback pairs with no omitted floor, the start is 4/F and final full landing is 2/F. This report independently verifies the start segment and first plaque only; full four-flight continuity is audited by the video agent.

factual_coordinate_relationship.frame: Current teaching-local u along classroom row toward the right/east end, v from corridor toward mountain/interior, h up.
factual_coordinate_relationship.approach_to_left_stair: -u along corridor; then turn toward +v into stair.
factual_coordinate_relationship.contradiction_with_retired_builder: Old build_walkthrough.py put its first ascending +v flight on side=+1, i.e. larger u, and copied that to WestStair. Video03 shows the opposite handedness. Do not restore the old flight order.

Neither old blocker v=33.05 nor old first riser v=36.5 is a photographed coordinate.
The current 5.76m clear shell width must not dictate flight widths.

safe_build_scope: Retain validated visible shape/direction as a research fragment. The probable plaque and unmeasured footprint do not justify constructing a site-positioned numbered-floor staircase under the user strict uncertainty rule. Do not extrapolate G..6 or copy the retired stairs.
mutations: Only new research frames, crops, scripts and this JSON created. No UE/project model changes.
